relevance_note: Case report of a Chilean proband with familial LCAT deficiency features and her four first-degree relatives, all genotyped: "In the proband, we found a compound heterozygous genotype with p.V333 M and p.M404 V mutations".
method_note: Written by a short Python script from my own reading; all spans checked verbatim by script. Labels: the proband is the single patient ('patient', rule 5); relatives are 'father/mother/sister/brother of patient' (rule 2); the paper gives no pedigree labels in text. The synonymous p.L393 L / p.L363 L (rs5923) variant was left out: the authors dismiss it as non-causal ('it is very unlikely that this variant has an important effect'); the family members carrying it are not individually stated beyond the proband ('found in the family under study in heterozygous state'). Contradictions/typos in the paper: the synonymous variant is called p.L363 L in the Abstract and Background but p.L393 L (c.1188C > T) in Results and Discussion; HEK-239 T vs HEK-293 T; proband HDL-cholesterol given as 3 mg/dL and also as 'undetectable'. Parental origin of the proband's variants is recorded as inherited maternal (p.V333 M) and inherited paternal (p.M404 V) from the statement that the mother carries p.V333 M and the father p.M404 V. cDNA strings (c.997G > A, c.1210A > G) printed in Methods/Results are used as variant_original_string; protein strings are given as p.V333 M / p.M404 V (also printed as p.Val333Met / p.Met404Val in Table 1). The paper notes p.V333 M was also referred to as p.V309 M (mature-protein numbering). No transcript printed. Variant type 'missense' comes from Table 1's 'Mutation type' column for each variant. Pathogenicity 'causative' is recorded only for the proband's rows (the sentence is about the proband); relatives' rows left not reported. In vitro HEK-293 T results are about the exact variant and were added to every carrier's row; plasma LCAT activity reductions are per relative (stated with 'respectively'). Relatives: 'normal plasma lipid profile' and 'without any clinical features of total or partial LCAT deficiency' are whole-investigation statements, recorded as such (excluded) without excluding specific checklist items; low HDL cholesterol is excluded from the separate statement 'relatives show normal plasma HDL-cholesterol levels'. Relatives' ages are 'at the time of the study' and recorded as age at last evaluation; the proband's age 36 is her age at ascertainment in 2009. cohort_size_as_stated left null: the GOCS population cohort (741/848 children; 57 low-HDL subjects screened negative for both variants) is a separate population analysis, not patients of this study. Fig. 1 (pedigree) not available as text.
